newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower, pressure on select stocks.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower, pressure on select stocks.

text.p: Swiss shares ended one percent lower, continuing Tuesday's consolidation, as derivatives-related selling and the easing dollar put pressure on some high-profile Swiss stocks.

Dealers said investors have grown cautious following the recent five-day bull run on the Swiss bourse, but fundamentals were seen favourable. One trader said the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) may reach 6,000 points in the next few months.
The SMI ended down 53.3 points, or 0.99 percent, to 5,308.6 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 19.46 points, or 0.57 percent, at 3,371.88.
Bourse volume reached 2.46 billion Swiss francs.
Actively-traded Novartis, which has been sought in the last few session at the expense of Roche, slid 36 francs, or 1.76 percent, to 2,011. Roche certificates were down 65 francs to 13,045.
The bourse was also pressured by a fall in Nestle, which was traded ex-dividend of 30 francs today. The stock ended off 41 francs to 1,814.
CS Group, which has recently lost ground as various rumours about alliances and spin-offs failed to materialise, added 0.75 francs to 192.25.

Sulzer shares continued a recent surge, adding 25 francs to 1,305. Traders said the stock was helped by speculation the conditions for the planned flotation of Sulzer Medica unit would be favourable for Sulzer shareholders.
Inspection firm SGS, which has been on the losing side recently, fell another 80 francs to 3,000.

Alusuisse, ABB and financials SBC, Winterthur and Baloise were among the day's winners. Alusuisse, whose Lonza Biologics unit said it planned to cooperate on devoping a therapeutic protein with U.S. firm Eli Lilly, ended up 20 francs to 1,462.
Insurer Zurich lost one francs to 558. Zurich said at Wednesday's annual meeting it expected a good 1997 result.
Komax, which was traded for the first time, was quoted at 541 francs compared to an issue price of 435.
